observation.visible_scene: A macro/zoom view of a tightly packed cluster of iridescent soap bubbles (blue, cyan, orange, yellow, magenta thin-film colors) on a black background, framed by a circular dark vignette that cuts in from the right. A screen-locked HUD overlay shows corner brackets with the text 'SOAP BUBBLES' (top-left), '%100' (top-right), 'MICRO ASMR / STEREOKROMA' (bottom-left), and a muted-sound icon (bottom-right); these stay at fixed pixel positions throughout.
visible_changes: The bubble cluster drifts slowly and continuously toward the left and slightly downward across the frame: e.g., the large top teardrop bubble moves from roughly x≈380 in the first frame to x≈300 by the last, and the leftmost orange bubble shifts from x≈105 to x≈40.
The internal thin-film colors within individual bubbles morph over time (swirling orange/blue/yellow patches change shape and position), indicating ongoing film flow rather than static coloring.
The black gap-network between bubbles widens and narrows as neighboring bubbles jostle and deform relative to one another, but the overall packing topology of the cluster is preserved.

The dark circular vignette on the right grows/shifts leftward, progressively occluding right-edge bubbles (e.g., orange bubbles at the top-right and mid-right become covered), which is occlusion by the dark region, not bubble disappearance.
The HUD text and icons remain completely stationary relative to the frame while the bubble content moves beneath them.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the leftward drift is bubble motion, camera pan/rotation, or both (the fixed HUD prevents using it as a reference).
What causes the vignette edge to advance and whether the cluster eventually leaves the illuminated area.
Any earlier triggering event or later outcome beyond this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Object motion vs. camera motion cannot be separated: the cluster's translation and the vignette's expansion could each be scene movement or viewpoint movement.
The slight apparent tilt/rotation of the cluster is small and could be a side effect of the circular vignette cropping rather than true rotation.
Color changes inside bubbles are real film interference shifts but their physical cause (draining, flow, lighting angle) is not determinable from the frames.

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
